issues.legal_issue: The civil-procedure rules governing suits do not have to be followed strictly in statutory proceedings before a District Judge when the governing law requires their application only so far as applicable.
material_facts: An allottee appealed to a District Judge against an order directing demolition of licensed shops.
The District Judge rejected the allottee’s application to record evidence.
The governing provision directed that civil-suit procedure be followed, as far as applicable, in applications, appeals, and references before the District Judge.
issues.conclusion: The appeal did not have to follow the procedure of a civil suit strictly. The Code of Civil Procedure provides guidance to be applied as far as appropriate to the proceedings; in an appropriate case, the District Judge may allow evidence to be led under Order 41, Rule 27.
issues.legal_principle: Section 384 of the Punjab Municipal Corporation Act, 1976, makes the Code of Civil Procedure’s procedure for suits applicable to proceedings before the District Judge only so far as it can be made applicable. The provision does not require applications, appeals, or references to follow suit procedure technically and strictly; relevant provisions concerning suits or appeals may guide the procedure. In an appropriate case, Order 41, Rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure may be applied to permit additional evidence. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

predicates.statutory_district_judge_appeal: A party brings an appeal under a statute before a District Judge.
predicates.qualified_civil_procedure_direction: The governing law directs that civil-suit procedure be followed in proceedings before the District Judge only insofar as it is applicable.
predicates.civil_procedure_guides_but_is_not_strict: Civil-procedure rules guide the proceeding but need not be followed strictly.

issues.definition: When a statutory appeal is brought before a District Judge and the governing law makes civil-suit procedure applicable only insofar as appropriate, civil procedure guides the proceeding without being strictly mandatory.
